problem: .handoff/RESUME.md says the bigint-money wave (migration 20261012140000_money_bigint) must merge first. That wave owns the schema money columns, lib/prisma.ts, accounting, reconciliation and reports. Raast's migrations are named 20261012130000 and 20261012130100, so they sort BEFORE 140000. If bigint ships first, prod gets an out-of-order migration. The new money columns (RaastReceipt amount/tip/due, BankSmsAlert.amountCents) are declared Int, so they either miss the BigInt conversion or disagree with it. Streams C and D edit the same files bigint is rewriting (accounting/orderPosting, shiftPosting, reconciliation/service.ts importBankStatement, reports/service, accounting/routes period close), so this is an overlapping build stream.
change: Make Raast depend on the merged bigint schema. Rename the migrations to timestamps after 20261012140000 (e.g. 20261013090000_raast_enum_values and 20261013090100_raast_tender). Type every new money column to bigint's convention for the column class it mirrors (Payment.amountCents and BankStatementLine.amountCents after bigint). Also reuse bigint's number<->BigInt read helper in the new code. Stream S starts only after bigint is merged to main, and C/D rebase on it. Add this ordering to §10.

problem: §6.5 step 4 race. An SMS is processed under the per-company advisory lock, but the cashier's POST /pos/raast/intents/:id/confirm (and POST /pos/payments with a typed ref) never takes that lock. So step 1 can find no receipt with the bankRef and step 3 can find the intent 'awaiting', while the cashier's transaction is still uncommitted. processPayment then waits on lockOrderTx and comes back ALREADY_PAID or RAAST_INTENT_GONE. The spec maps any AppError refusal to 'receipt needs_attention (attentionReason=code)'. That overwrites the receipt the cashier just made provisional with a paymentId. Every reader that filters on provisional|matched then drops a paid sale: chooseRaastRefundSourceTx, the statement pre-pass (provisional|unreceived) and the flags. The alert also goes needs_attention instead of 'confirmed'.
change: In applyBankCredit, before marking anything after a refusal, re-read the receipt and order under the lock. If the receipt is now provisional or matched with an equal amount, run the step-1 path instead (linkAlertTx 'confirmed', smsConfirmedAt). Only write needs_attention with a conditional updateMany where status IN ('awaiting') and the id matches, never an unconditional update by id. Make every Raast write path take the same per-company lock first: cashier confirm, POST /pos/payments raast, attach, the reference fix and intent cancel/expiry. Add a test: cashier confirm and SMS for the same intent at the same moment leave one payment, the receipt provisional with smsAlertId set, and the alert 'confirmed'.

problem: §6.5 serialises applyBankCredit with pg_advisory_xact_lock and then calls processPayment/settlePayment in step 4. Those open their OWN prisma.$transaction on a second pooled connection and then run afterTillSale (completeOrder, fiscal filing, loyalty) after commit. The outer interactive transaction stays open across all of that. Prisma's default interactive-tx timeout is 5 s, while processPayment alone allows maxWait 10 s and timeout 15 s. If the outer transaction expires after the inner payment committed, the alert's 'matched' write is lost and the alert falls back to received/duplicate. Several companies' SMS in flight at once each hold one connection and wait for a second, which can starve the pool.
change: Do not hold an interactive transaction across processPayment. Option 1: in a short transaction (xact advisory lock, candidate search, atomically claim the intent with a 'settling' marker, e.g. smsAlertId set plus a lease timestamp, and the alert set to 'processing'), commit, then call processPayment/settlePayment with the intent id, then finish the alert in a second short transaction. Option 2: take a session-level pg_advisory_lock on a dedicated connection and release it in finally. Specify which one in §6.5. The processPayment intent claim must accept the 'settling' marker held by the same alert.

problem: Fraud hole in the cross-checks. findSmsForRefTx (§4.1) and step 1 (§6.5) match on (tenantId, bankRef) plus amount only. They do not check the alert's bankAccountId against the receipt's receiving account, the alert's age, or its status. So a reference from a credit a manager DISMISSED as 'not a sale' (supplier refund, owner transfer) can be typed by a cashier on a bill of the same amount. The receipt then shows as SMS-confirmed, the raast_unconfirmed flag never fires, and the statement pre-pass later matches it to that genuine non-sale credit. The cashier pockets the customer's cash and the books look clean. Credits on another of the company's bank accounts, 'debit' alerts and days-old 'off' alerts can be borrowed the same way. The finance PATCH /receipts/:id/reference (FINANCE_TEAM) can re-point a receipt the same way.
change: findSmsForRefTx, step 1 and the statement pre-pass may only use credit alerts and lines that meet all of these: kind credit; status in (received, processing, unmatched, ambiguous, off, needs_attention); bankAccountId equal to the receipt's bankAccountId; occurredAt within [receipt.createdAt − matchWindowMin, now]. If the ref belongs to a dismissed or debit alert of the company: 409 RAAST_REF_DISMISSED on the payment, and the statement pre-pass skips it. Persist dismissed refs as a per-company claim (e.g. a nullable BankSmsAlert.claimedRef with @@unique([tenantId, claimedRef]) checked together with RaastReceipt) so one transfer can never be both 'not a sale' and a sale. Move PATCH /reconciliation/raast/receipts/:id/reference to APPROVERS with the same checks, and audit before/after.

problem: matchOnIntentCreated auto-settles a new intent with an unmatched credit whose occurredAt is up to matchWindowMin (10 min) BEFORE the intent existed. That credit was by definition sent before this bill was put up for Raast. Typically it is another customer's payment for a bill the cashier never put in Raast mode, often at another location sharing the same receiving account and SIM. Auto-attaching it marks a bill paid whose customer has not paid, which the owner's 'never guess' rule forbids.
change: On intent creation, auto-settle only alerts with occurredAt >= intent.createdAt − clockSkewMin (2 min). Older unmatched alerts with the same amount are shown on the RaastPanel as 'possible earlier payment: PKR X from <payer> at hh:mm', and the cashier attaches one with the existing attach action. Test: an SMS 5 minutes before the intent never settles it on its own.

problem: The existing /webhooks/pos plugin keys its rate limit on params.token. Copied to POST /webhooks/pos/sms (token in the Authorization header), the key becomes the empty string, so every company's devices share ONE 120/min bucket and a single busy or abusive caller blocks all bank SMS. Separately, the path-token fallback /webhooks/pos/sms/:deviceToken puts a live bearer credential into Fastify request logs (pino logs req.url; only req.headers.authorization is redacted in index.ts) and into Cloudflare logs. Unauthenticated garbage tokens also cost one DB lookup each.
change: Key the SMS route on sha256(token) from the header (or the path), plus an IP-keyed limit for failed auths. Add a req serializer or redact rule that masks /webhooks/pos/sms/<token> in logged URLs, and put the fallback behind a per-device flag 'allowPathToken' (default off), shown in RaastSetup with the log warning. Look up active devices by tokenHash only after a cheap format check (/^sms_[0-9a-f]{64}$/).

problem: §7.1 runs the generic matcher after the Raast pre-pass over the same lines. A Raast credit whose reference is not found in the statement text falls through to it, and it pairs that credit with ANY equal-amount debit journal line on the bank code within 3 days (a cash deposit, a manual entry). The line becomes 'matched' to the wrong entry, so the Raast receipt can never be matched (POST /receipts/:id/match requires an unmatched line) and stays flagged as raast_unmatched. reconciliation/routes.ts has no route to undo a generic match. Banks often print a different ID on the statement (RRN/STAN) than in the SMS or merchant app, so ref misses will be common, and Raast adds many small credits at typical bill amounts.
change: In the generic pass on an import whose bankAccountId receives Raast (default or any brand override), skip positive lines that equal the amount of a provisional receipt on that account within ±statementMatchDays and leave them for the Raast tab. Add POST /reconciliation/bank/lines/:id/unmatch (APPROVERS, audited) to clear a generic match. In the Raast tab, offer 'exactly one provisional receipt with the same amount and day, no ref hit' as a SUGGESTED match that finance confirms, never as an auto-match.

problem: The 'same transfer can't pay two bills' rule is @@unique([tenantId, bankRef]). BankAccount rows are per company, so if two companies (shared head-office setup) register the same IBAN or Raast ID as their receiving account, a cashier in company B can claim company A's transfer reference. Each company then imports its own copy of the same statement and matches it, so one transfer is counted as revenue and bank money in both books.
change: In PATCH /setup/bank-accounts (raastDefault) and PUT /setup/raast-accounts, refuse with 409 RAAST_ACCOUNT_SHARED when another company's active BankAccount with the same normalised iban, accountNumber or raastId is already a Raast receiving account (default or brand override). State the rule in CLAUDE.md. If the owner later wants shared accounts, the claim becomes unique on (normalised IBAN, bankRef) across companies. Test with two companies.

problem: Two gaps in the keenu_qr retirement. (1) A pre-deploy check split with one portion already paid and a pending keenu_qr portion left: settle answers 422 KEENU_QR_RETIRED with the advice 're-split', but prepareSplitTx refuses to re-split any bill with a paid portion (ALREADY_PAID), so the advice is a dead end. (2) The printed Keenu QR standees stay on counters after deploy. A customer who pays to the Keenu QR can only be recorded as 'card' (which is correct: the money arrives via Keenu at 1030), but nothing tells the cashier so.
change: (1) Make the KEENU_QR_RETIRED message on settle say 'take the rest with Pay (cash, Card – Keenu or Raast QR)'. processPayment on the remainder already fails the leftover pending row in applyCoverageTx; add a test for exactly this flow. (2) Have RaastPanel or the cutover notice say 'A payment made to the old Keenu QR is recorded as Card – Keenu', and add 'remove the Keenu QR standees at deploy' to docs/raast.md and the deploy checklist.

problem: §7.4 counts provisional|needs_attention receipts with confirmedAt <= lock date. A receipt that went needs_attention from an intent (SMS amount differs, refusal) has confirmedAt NULL, so it never blocks the close even though the customer's money is in the bank unbooked. The guard also only blocks 'awaiting' receipts. Once an intent is needs_attention, the cashier can take cash for the bill, which then completes and leaves the attention receipt (and any targetPaymentId pointing at a pending split row that writePortions later deletes) open with no owner.
change: Period close: count receipts in (provisional, needs_attention) with COALESCE(confirmedAt, createdAt) <= lockedThrough. When an order completes by another tender while it has a needs_attention receipt, raise or refresh raast_needs_attention for finance with 'bill settled otherwise; customer transfer PKR X to refund or attach'. Clear targetPaymentId when writePortions deletes the row it points at (or skip pending rows referenced by a live receipt).

problem: §10 puts mkRaastAccount(co, opts) in tests/connectorsFixtures.ts, owned by stream B, but streams A and D write tests against it in parallel. They will either invent their own copies (a second fixture) or fail to compile until B lands.
change: Move the mkRaastAccount helper (BankAccount with accountCode linked in the company's chart, raastDefault, optional brand override) and the payments-union change in connectorsFixtures.ts into stream S's serial contract step, written before the fan-out.
